name: Bucharest Henri Coandă International Airport
before:
Romania's busiest airport, at Otopeni 16.5 km north of central Bucharest, handling over 17 million passengers in 2025. It is the headquarters and hub for TAROM and a base for HiSky, Animawings, FlyOne, Ryanair and Wizz Air.

The layout confuses people because the three parts are called terminals but are one building. Departures and Arrivals are separate halls joined by a walkway lined with shops, and the Finger Terminal is the airside concourse, split into domestic and international flows. Between them there are 104 check in desks and 38 gates, of which 14 have jetways.

There is a railway station by the Arrivals hall car park with trains to Gara de Nord running 24 hours a day, operated by CFR and Transferoviar Călători.

Two parallel runways serve the airport, both 3,500 metres.

Bucharest's other airport is the smaller Băneasa Aurel Vlaicu, inside the city. This one was a military airfield until 1965, took civilian traffic from 1969 and was renamed in 2004 after Henri Coandă, who built the Coandă-1910 aircraft and discovered the Coandă effect.
after:
Romania's busiest airport, at Otopeni, 16.5 km north of central Bucharest. It handled about 17 million passengers in 2025. Ryanair has a base here.

Trains run from the airport's own station to Gara de Nord, Bucharest's main railway station.

Two parallel runways serve the airport, both 3,500 metres long.

Bucharest's other airport, Băneasa Aurel Vlaicu, is inside the city.

claims.claim: over 17 million in 2025; TAROM headquarters and hub; bases for HiSky, Animawings, FlyOne, Ryanair and Wizz Air
claims.wasBefore: Romania's busiest airport, at Otopeni 16.5 km north of central Bucharest, handling over 17 million passengers in 2025. It is the headquarters and hub for TAROM and a base for HiSky, Animawings, FlyOne, Ryanair and Wizz Air.
claims.why: Reworded: the position, the traffic (as 'about 17 million') and the Ryanair base are kept. TAROM's headquarters and hub and the other four airlines' bases rest on Wikipedia alone: the airport's site refused (403), TAROM's about page is a 404 and its contact page gives no head office.

claims.claim: layout: Departures, Arrivals and Finger 'terminals' are one building; 104 desks, 38 gates, 14 jetways
claims.wasBefore: The layout confuses people because the three parts are called terminals but are one building. Departures and Arrivals are separate halls joined by a walkway lined with shops, and the Finger Terminal is the airside concourse, split into domestic and international flows. Between them there are 104 check in desks and 38 gates, of which 14 have jetways.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the operator's site refused both a plain request and the browser (403).

claims.claim: railway station by the Arrivals car park; trains 24 hours a day by CFR and Transferoviar Călători
claims.wasBefore: There is a railway station by the Arrivals hall car park with trains to Gara de Nord running 24 hours a day, operated by CFR and Transferoviar Călători.
claims.why: Reworded: the station and the trains to Gara de Nord are kept with CFR as the second source. 'Twenty-four hours', the car park position and Transferoviar rest on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: smaller Băneasa; military airfield until 1965; civilian from 1969; renamed 2004 after Henri Coandă
claims.wasBefore: Bucharest's other airport is the smaller Băneasa Aurel Vlaicu, inside the city. This one was a military airfield until 1965, took civilian traffic from 1969 and was renamed in 2004 after Henri Coandă, who built the Coandă-1910 aircraft and discovered the Coandă effect.
claims.why: Băneasa inside the city is kept (OurAirports). 'Smaller' and the whole history rest on Wikipedia alone.
